name: APEX DRIFT: Corponation Aerial Racing Championship
description: Pilots in exo-frame wing rigs — partially augmented, partially mechanical — race through a three-dimensional course threaded between Meridian 88's upper Stack towers, using a combination of physical reflexes, BCI-linked navigation systems, and onboard machine logic to navigate 200-kilometer circuits at speeds exceeding 600 kph. APEX DRIFT is fully owned and operated by Axiom Network's sport division, with eight corporate-sponsored teams bearing livery from Axiom subsidiaries and two 'independent wild card' teams who exist primarily to be beaten. The championship final is the second most-watched single sporting event in Meridian 88 each year.
story_hooks: A Shelf rooftop-watching community that has tracked APEX DRIFT races for years notices a pattern in 'accidental' course deviations that always seem to damage the same district's infrastructure.
The sole genuine independent wild card team — funded by a Tier 2 collective — actually wins a qualifying round, and Axiom's behind-the-scenes response reveals how deeply the competition is managed.

A retired APEX DRIFT champion is hired as a consultant by a Shelf engineer trying to adapt racing exo-frame technology into cheap civilian transport, and the corponation that owns the IP sends someone to stop them.
